$comment: Capability registry of Frontend Architect (1.5, increment 1). Capabilities name what a frontend task needs; every capability has an internal owner (a skill or agent of this plugin) that always applies. External integrations are optional collaborators: the registry says how each one is recognised on disk, which capabilities it can help with, what it runs and what it needs. Nothing in this file is executed; scripts/capabilities.mjs reads it and the skill text explains how to use the result. Order matters: integrations are listed by increasing risk, and that order breaks ties.

capabilities.what: art direction, typography, colour, composition, the look and feel that fits product, user and context
tokens, theming, component conventions, density modes, UI states
building screens, forms, tables and components with the project's library and conventions
reviewing an existing interface: hierarchy, spacing, typography, colour, consistency, anti-patterns
refining details, micro-interactions and states without changing the structure
layout across viewports, text scale and density; verified with browser-audit
names, roles, keyboard, focus, contrast, forms; static ui-audit and opt-in browser-audit evidence
animation and scroll choreography with lifecycle, reduced-motion and performance rules; the official GSAP skills may collaborate when GSAP is named or already a dependency
Three.js, TresJS, React Three Fiber, shaders, WebGL/WebGPU with fallbacks and disposal
stage, structure, state, API layer, contracts, SSR safety, security, performance budgets
rendered-page evidence: axe-core, keyboard, dialogs, forms, responsive, visual regression (opt-in, authorised URL)

integrations.runs: prose only: one SKILL.md, no scripts, no tools, no network
npx impeccable <command>: downloads and executes a package; a live browser server for the live command; its frontmatter grants Bash(npx impeccable *) without a permission prompt for the turn
integrations.writes: PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, .impeccable/ and .impeccable-live* inside the project
preconditions: the user accepts that npx runs a package from the network
the user accepts files written into the project

integrations.runs: python3 scripts that search bundled CSV data; image-generation features need GEMINI_API_KEY (network, paid API)
integrations.writes: design-system files it generates in the project when asked
preconditions: python3 on PATH for its search scripts
never set or share API keys on its behalf; image generation is out of scope

integrations.subcapability: core API: to/from/fromTo, easing, stagger, matchMedia

policy.selection: for each needed capability that allows external help, the available integration covering the most needed capabilities wins; ties go to registry order; at most maxExternal distinct integrations per plan, the rest are listed as alternatives or deferred
policy.evidence: a collaborator is recommended, never run, by this tool; execution exists only when the session shows a Skill tool invocation of that skill and its result
policy.precedence: the user's instructions and the project's conventions override any collaborator; the internal owner arbitrates conflicts; collaborators produce suggestions, not decisions
policy.groups: integrations with the same group count as one toward maxExternal; a group may contribute several skills up to its maxPerPlan

gsap.label: official GSAP skills (greensock/gsap-skills, MIT, prose only)
gsap.gate: the task names GSAP, ScrollTrigger or GreenSock, or the project depends on gsap; otherwise motion stays internal (CSS, View Transitions, Motion first)
gsap.selection: skills whose sub-capability keywords match the task, most matches first, then registry order; gsap-core only when nothing specific matches; the project framework adds gsap-react (react/next) or gsap-frameworks (vue/nuxt/svelte)
